states.label: A · Review, 1200 pt window: the pointer is on the gap between the details and the Conversation (automatic width, 300 pt)
B · Dragging left: the Conversation is 440 pt and the details give way; saved when you let go
C · A smaller window (1060 pt): the details keep 360 pt, so the Conversation stops at 352 pt; the handle turns peach
D · Below 780 pt of content (a 980 pt window): today’s rule, the Conversation sits behind a button and there is nothing to drag
E · History → Jobs, three columns, two handles: hover on the list’s edge (a 1 pt line today); the Conversation has its own
F · Actions → To do: dragging the detail wider (420 pt) from the list’s edge
Every split screen: what you drag, its limits, and what stays
states.caption: One key per row in Distill’s UI preferences (distill.pane.…). A missing key is the automatic width, so nothing looks different until you drag.

states.caption: Same on every screen. The mechanism is one SwiftUI modifier, so the narrow-window rules and the snapshots keep working.

boards.title: Resizable panes · drag the divider between two columns
boards.heading: Resizable panes: drag the line between two columns
boards.intro: “For any UI with the open left section, I am able to change the size.” Every screen with two or three columns gets a handle on the boundary between them: Review and its Conversation, History, Actions, Activity, Collectors, the Settings nav and the sidebar. Hover shows the resize cursor and a grip; drag to resize; double-click for the automatic width. Each column has a min and a max, and the other column always keeps room. Widths are remembered per screen across restarts. Nothing changes until you drag: the automatic widths are today’s widths, and today’s narrow-window rules stay.
